thread:
Alex M: incident-bot just paged P1 - sudden increase in runtime tail latency (99p > 2.5s) and queue depth rising across us-west-2. Seeing big queue spikes on gen and chat routes. :warning:
incident-bot: [PAGER] P1 - high tail latency on runtime (service: runtime-api-usw2). Alert triggered at 2101234567. Pager duty: on-call.eng. Link: https://incidents.redwood/runtime/2101234567
Priya S: Confirming, dashboards show avg queue depth from ~50 -> 900 in 5m. Error budget burn for hosted tier rising.
Jamal R: Any obvious traffic spike? Logs show a noisy customer sending long chat contexts, lots of streaming connections.
Dana K: Correlating with a spike in embedding batch jobs too. Looks like a scheduled job from acct_prod-17 started at 2101234540 and iteratively retried.
Alex M: Ok first mitigations we can do quickly: 1) lower runtime.max_in_flight global to shed load, 2) enable shedding for low-priority endpoints (analytics, preview embeddings), 3) temporary per-customer rate limit on acct_prod-17. I'll start with max_in_flight.
Megan L: +1 do the quick config changes. We should prefer failing fast over long queuing.
Alex M: Running command now:
```
# reduce global max in-flight to shrink queue pressure
adminctl runtime config set --key max_in_flight --value 400 --env prod --reason "emergency backpressure"
```
incident-bot: Config change requested by Alex M: runtime.max_in_flight -> 400. Change will roll to 3 runtime clusters.
Priya S: Traffic telemetry: after first cluster update, queue depth dropped from 900 -> 320 in that cluster, 95p latency dropping. Still high on two other clusters.
Jamal R: I'll apply per-customer soft-rate-limit for acct_prod-17: throttle to 200 reqs/min and drop large streaming contexts above 2048 tokens.
Alex M: Command for throttling (Jamal go ahead):
```
curl -X POST "https://console.redwood/api/admin/quotas" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"customer_id":"acct_prod-17","rate_limit_rpm":200,"max_context_tokens":2048}'
```
Dana K: Also toggling feature flag to disable embeddings-preview which is spiking memory and blocking workers.
```
ffctl toggle --flag embeddings-preview --env prod --value off --actor "Dana K" --note "emergency mitigation - heavy mem usage"
```
Ryan C: Heads up: disabling that flag will cause some customers to fallback to cached embeddings. Monitor 429s.
Megan L: Good. Also set request timeout lower so slow streaming clients don't hold sockets: change runtime.request_timeout from 30s -> 6s for non-committed routes.
Alex M: Doing that now:
```
adminctl runtime config patch --path /routes/*/request_timeout --value 6000 --env prod --scope non_committed
```
Luis P: After the first wave of changes (max_in_flight + throttle + ff off) we see overall queue depth down 70% and 99p latency for gen routes is now ~1.3s. Hosted error rate still slightly elevated due to retries.
Priya S: Noted several customers hitting 429s — mainly low-tier webhooks and analytics pipelines now getting throttled. Customer-impact list: acct_prod-17 (noisy job), acct_salesforce-sync (background), acct_free-tier-42 (webhooks).
Jamal R: For acct_prod-17 I applied an emergency quota and sent them a soft-notification email and webhook to ops contact. They acknowledged and will reschedule.
Alex M: Next steps: 1) keep throttles in place for 30m, 2) monitor SLOs for hosted and dedicated, 3) prepare rollback plan if we overshoot. I'll hand off to Priya for monitoring.
Priya S: On it — I'll watch the NOC dashboard and keep updates every 5m. If queue depth <200 for 2 consecutive 5m windows, start ramping max_in_flight back up in +50 increments with 1m waits.
Megan L: Agree. Also open a follow-up ticket to implement smarter per-tenant rate limiting at the edge and circuit-breakers per route.
Dana K: Capturing commands used and times in incident ticket. Also let's keep the embeddings-preview flag disabled until we validate memory back to baseline.
Alex M: Handoff: I'm going offline in 20m; Priya you're primary. @Priya S please escalate to eng-runtime if we see any regression.
Priya S: Acknowledged. I'll page if 99p > 2s again or error rate > 2%.
Luis P: Postmortem note: likely combination of scheduled noisy batch + insufficient per-tenant controls + large default max_in_flight that allowed long queues. We'll propose default max_in_flight per-region and per-route caps.
Jamal R: One more tweak: added a temporary route rule to prefer dedicated nodes for long streaming sessions to avoid starving gen workers.
Alex M: Thanks team. I'll draft the incident summary and impact note for customers (who saw increased latencies and throttles).
incident-bot: Incident P1 (2101234567) acknowledged by Alex M, assigned to Priya S for monitoring. Incident state: mitigated -> active monitoring.
Priya S: Update at 2101234740: all clusters stable, queue depths <150, 99p latency at ~1.1s. Leaving throttles on for another 15m then start controlled ramp.
Megan L: :thumbsup: good job. Follow-up owners: eng-runtime (Jamal, Dana) for config hardening; platform (Megan, Luis) for per-tenant limits; oncall rotate to normal schedule in 30m.
Alex M: Closing notes: customers impacted were throttled but not dropped wholesale; we disabled an expensive feature flag, lowered timeouts, reduced max_in_flight, and applied per-tenant quotas. Will run retro tomorrow.
Priya S: last update 2101234780 — monitoring window complete, leaving incident in resolved state, will file a postmortem with timeline and proposed mitigations. :white_check_mark:
